The orientation of the columnar grain is about 4° deviating from <001> orientation (Fig. 9d).

In addition, grain rotation occurs d uring tensile deformation [21]. The columnar grains with similar orientation rotate around the axis of <001> direction (Fig. 9), while the rotation direction of fine grains with different crystal orientations is random.
The deformation incompatibility between fine-grain region and columnar-grain region also result in the change of stress field near the interface, as illustrated in the previous study [8].

Rotation direction of fine -grain region and c olumnar-grain region of dual structure superalloys is different during tensile deformation. Larger tensile strain may be accumulated near the transition zone between fine-grain region and columnar-grain region, which is confirmed by the severe surface d eformation in dual structure specimens (Fig. 8b).

In columnar-grain specimen with <001> orientation, the different slip bands result in the stress concentration near the MC carbides or micro-pores (Fig. 7c), and transgranular cracks are initiated (Fig. 8c)

In addition, intergranular cracks were initiated with the intersection between grain boundaries and SBs (Fig. 7b). Moreover, grain boundary cracks form preferentially due to the low strength of grain boundaries with increasing temperature (Fig. 8e)
